commercial_incentive: sells SAT/ACT prep and essay coaching (Ivy Lounge Test Prep); repeated plugs for a free masterclass and website
key_insights: Demonstrated interest acts mainly as a tiebreaker between similarly qualified applicants at highly selective schools with low admit rates
Colleges favor applicants likely to actually enroll, since accepting many who won't attend makes it hard to fill diverse campus roles
Five major ways to show interest: campus visit, official tour, info session, talking to a rep at a fair/school visit, and signing up for an interview if offered
Four tracked 'minor' ways: browsing the college website (time-on-site is monitored), following/engaging on social media, opening recruiting emails promptly, and clicking links inside them
Suggests keeping a separate, real-name 'clean' social media profile specifically for following and engaging with colleges
Demonstrated interest can tip close calls but does not replace strong grades, test scores, or essays
notable_or_distinctive: recommends creating a second, real-name social media alias purely to interact with colleges safely, a more paranoid/specific tactic than in other demonstrated-interest videos
reliability_notes: presenter is a test-prep marketer with no stated admissions-office credential; email/website tracking claims are plausible but unsourced, and the video is built around repeated self-promotion
